ideas.description: Exploit: spend the measured resize-vs-epoch rate gap on the Muon tip. E034 (40% at 24 px, 8.75 ep) bought +0.18 pp for +0.24 s, about 0.75 pp/s. Cutting epochs on the Muon line costs about 0.56 pp/s (E028 to E031: 0.23 pp for 0.41 s). Start from tip E031 (commit 3797e1a: Muon lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 on block convs, fused and graphed, 128/256/704, translate 2, LS 0.1, alternating flip, batch 2048, 8.75 ep). Change two settings together as one recipe point: the 24 px fraction goes from the first 50% to the first 40% of steps (the E034 setting), and epochs go from 8.75 to 8.0. Rescale the LR, Lookahead and Muon schedules to the new step count so they still anneal fully. Both shapes stay graphed in build. Report per-seed accuracy. If the 3-seed margin over 0.753 is under 0.3 pp, rerun once and pool before promoting it (H1.1.3 rule).
ideas.expected: Time about 5.18-5.28 s (E034's 5.67 s minus 0.75 ep at about 0.57 s/ep), 3-5% faster than E031's 5.43 s. Accuracy about 0.752-0.757, centred near 0.7546. If it is feasible after pooling, it is a new best, and it confirms that under Muon the frontier sits at a lower low-res fraction with fewer epochs (supports W34/W36's convex resize cost). If accuracy is below 0.751, the epoch curve steepens below 8.75 ep (a knee), and the next margin has to come from zero-cost levers.

ideas.description: New Lvl3 under H4.2, from D009 (C0094, C0095, C0099): a zero-cost accuracy-per-step lever. On tip E031, change only the Newton-Schulz polynomial coefficients. Replace the fixed airbench quintic (a, b, c) = (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) with Polar-Express-style per-iteration coefficients at the same iteration count. First confirm the current count in the code; E025's notes suggest 3. Keep the same pre-normalization, including the small safety factor, and keep bf16. Iteration count, momentum, lr, schedule and the stacked bmm grouping stay the same. Verify on a random 704x6336 matrix that the singular values after NS fall in [0.7, 1.2] before running.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.03 s), since the matmul count is identical. Accuracy +0.0 to +0.3 pp, to about 0.755-0.758. A gain of 0.2 pp or more, which is worth about 0.35 s of epochs at 0.56 pp/s, is spent on an epoch cut next. A gain under 0.1 pp means the small-singular-value speedup does not matter for this small CNN, which closes NS-coefficient tuning. In that case the follow-up is fewer iterations as a pure time lever.

ideas.description: Margin builder from E030's implication. Translate 4 hurt more under Muon (-0.62 pp) than under SGD (-0.35 pp), so the weak-augmentation optimum may sit below 2 px under Muon. On tip E031, change only the random-translate amplitude, from 2 px to 1 px (reflect padding as now) in both resolution phases. Everything else is fixed.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.03 s). Accuracy -0.25 to +0.35 pp, centred about +0.1. A gain of 0.2 pp or more means augmentation strength should keep falling with the budget under Muon (H4.1), and the margin goes to the epoch or resize combination. A loss of 0.2 pp or more puts the optimum at 2 px, and the translate axis is closed.

ideas.description: Noise floor on the actual tip, required by the H1.1.3 rule because E031's margin is +0.21 pp (< 0.3). Rerun E031 (commit 3797e1a) unchanged, once. Pool it with E031, and use E028 and E034 for context, to estimate the run-to-run sd of a 3-seed mean on the Muon line, where per-trial same-seed nondeterminism was up to 0.9 pp under SGD. Report per-seed accuracy and time.
ideas.expected: Time 5.43 ± 0.03 s. 3-seed accuracy 0.752-0.758, with a run-to-run difference of 0.3 pp or less. If the rerun falls below 0.753, E031 is not reliably feasible: the pooled mean becomes the incumbent's accuracy, and any time cut must first buy back margin. If the pooled sd of a 3-seed mean is 0.15 pp or less, single-run verdicts at a 0.3 pp margin can be trusted from here on.

ideas.description: Follow-up to E035, where removing Lookahead cost -0.81 pp, so averaging is first-order. Test stronger averaging. On tip E031, first read the Lookahead constants in the code (cadence k, peak decay, ramp exponent). Then change only the peak decay of the slow-weight update from 0.95**k to 0.97**k, which roughly doubles the averaging window in steps. Keep the same cubic ramp, cadence and final sync to the slow weights. The GPU alpha table changes; nothing else does.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.02 s). Accuracy -0.25 to +0.35 pp, centred about +0.1. A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports the post-mortem's claim that Lookahead stands in for the annealing that the 7%-floor schedule leaves incomplete under Muon's fixed-size steps. The next steps would then be a lower ramp exponent or an epoch cut. A loss of 0.2 pp or more means the averaging is already at its optimum strength and should be left alone.

ideas.description: Close the Muon lr axis from below. E033 showed that 0.32 was worse (-0.33 pp) at 8.75 ep and batch 2048, so the optimum is at or below 0.24. On tip E031, change only the Muon peak lr, from 0.24 to 0.18: same schedule shape, momentum 0.6, SGD groups unchanged. Only the GPU LR table changes.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged. Accuracy -0.35 to +0.25 pp. A gain of 0.15 pp or more means the short-horizon, large-batch optimum lies below the CIFAR-10 default (consistent with D007's C0053), and a momentum 0.5 test comes next. A loss of 0.2 pp or more brackets the optimum at about 0.24, which closes Muon lr tuning.

ideas.description: Explore width under Muon. Under Muon, block-2 FLOPs and the NS cost on block-2 filters are both per-step work, and Muon's higher sample efficiency may make block-2 capacity even less binding than under SGD (E012). On tip E031, change only the block-2 width, from 256 to 192 (128/192/704, 3 convs per block; block-3 conv1 input follows). Nothing else changes. Muon groups are re-formed for the new shapes, and graphs are recaptured in build.
ideas.expected: Time -0.25 to -0.40 s, to about 5.05-5.2 s: about 12% fewer conv MACs plus smaller NS matrices. Accuracy -0.15 to -0.5 pp. The rate in pp lost per second saved decides the outcome. Below 0.5 pp/s beats the epoch cut (0.56 pp/s), and narrowing block 2 becomes the next time lever, paired with a margin builder. Above 0.8 pp/s means block-2 width is binding at 256 under Muon, which closes the width axis.

ideas.description: Zero-cost schedule leftover from 37-epoch runs, re-posed on the Muon tip. At 8.75 ep, whiten_bias_epochs 3 trains the whitening bias for about 34% of the run. On tip E031, first confirm in the code that a whitening-bias phase exists and what its semantics are. If it does not exist, record a no-op and do not run. Otherwise change only whiten_bias_epochs, from 3 to 1 (scaled about 3/37 x 8.75 ≈ 0.7, rounded up).
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.02 s). Accuracy -0.2 to +0.3 pp. A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H4.5: schedule constants tuned for long runs are off at about 9 ep, and the margin goes to epochs. A change within ±0.15 pp closes this constant.

structured_output.summary:
Every queued idea is done or dropped, so there was nothing to drop and the queue was empty. I added 8 ideas, all on the Muon tip E031 (5.43 s, 0.7551, margin +0.21 pp).

**Top priority (5): a direct time cut.** It trades less resize for fewer epochs: 24 px fraction from 50% to 40%, epochs from 8.75 to 8.0. Under Muon the two levers now cost different amounts:
- Resize near 50% costs about 0.75 pp per second saved (E034).
- Cutting epochs costs about 0.56 pp per second saved (E028 to E031).

The projected point is about 5.2 s at about 0.7546, which is a thin margin. It runs under the rule that any keep with a margin under 0.3 pp is rerun and pooled before it becomes the tip.

**Priority 4: build margin at no extra time.**
- **New Newton-Schulz coefficients.** Swap the fixed quintic for per-iteration coefficients at the same iteration count. This comes from D009 and is the only zero-cost accuracy lever the literature offers.
- **Translate 2 px to 1 px.** E030 hit harder under Muon (-0.62 pp vs -0.35 pp under SGD), which suggests the augmentation optimum may sit below 2 px.
- **A required rerun of E031.** Its margin is under 0.3 pp, so the noise-floor rule calls for it.

**Priority 3: tune Muon's surroundings.**
- **Stronger Lookahead averaging** (peak decay 0.95**k to 0.97**k). E035 showed averaging is first-order: removing Lookahead cost -0.81 pp.
- **Muon lr down to 0.18.** E033 showed 0.32 was worse; this checks the other side of 0.24.

**Priority 2: explore.**
- **Block-2 width 256 to 192 under Muon.** It measures pp lost per second saved, against the 0.56 pp/s epoch rate.
- **Whitening-bias phase cut from 3 to 1 epoch.** This is a no-op if the phase doesn't exist in the code.

**How these settle what the world models disagree on.** The 40%/8.0 run and the block-2 cut test whether resize gets convexly more expensive above about 0.4 and whether the epoch curve has a knee below 8.75 ep. The averaging and lr ideas probe Muon-specific behaviour that none of the world models captures.
